newsitem.title: USA: Mattel has lower first quarter, hurt by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Mattel has lower first quarter, hurt by strong dollar.

text.p: Mattel Inc., the world's largest toy company, Thursday reported lower first quarter earnings, citing the impact of the strong dollar as well as expenses related to its recent acquisition of Tyco Toys Inc.
Sales of Barbie, Mattel's most famous doll, were up 10 percent and sales of Disney products rose more than 20 percent. Hot Wheels sales nearly doubled, Mattel said.
However, sales of Fisher-Price toys fell 29 percent from a year earlier.

Mattel reported net income of $13 million, or five cents a share for the 1997 first quarter, before accounting for its merger with Tyco Toys and the impact of a charge related to integration and restructuring.
Mattel had earlier indicated that it expected first quarter earnings to be in the range of one cent to four cents a share.
The current quarter's bottom line was hurt by the strength of the U.S. dollar, which makes both production and sale of its products overseas more expensive.
A year earlier, Mattel earned $29.9 million, or 11 cents a share.
First quarter net sales for Mattel, without the impact of Tyco sales, were $569 million, down 3 percent from $586 million in the year-ago quarter.
Tyco, the maker of last Christmas' hottest toy, Tickle Me Elmo, was acquired March 31.

Consolidated earnings for Mattel and Tyco were one cent per share before a pre-tax charge of $275 million related to the Tyco integration and Mattel restructuring, which is expected to result in savings of $700 million over the next five years.

"Tyco products were also in strong demand, with a sales increase of 27 percent led by the strength of the Tyco core brands of Sesame Street, Matchbox and Magna Doodle," said Jill Barad, Mattel's president and chief executive officer.

"Our integration and restructuring activities are well under way, and will result in global growth opportunities and pre-tax savings of $60 million this year and $160 million per year in 1998 and beyond," she said. "We remain solidly on track to achieve our full-year targets for 1997."
Mattel has its headquarters in El Segundo, Calif., manufacturing facilities in 36 countries and sells its products in more than 140 nations throughout the world.
Mattel stock was up $1.25 at $26.25 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
